title: Boundary localization triangle for a curve
statement:
Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a dense open immersion of smooth
curves, let $i:Z_0=C_0\setminus U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$, and let
$\mathcal F$ be lisse on $U_0$. The open–closed localization
triangle, with the middle extension of [def-wf-middle-extension],
gives

$$
R\Gamma_c(U,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow
R\Gamma_c(C,j_*\mathcal F)\longrightarrow
R\Gamma_c(Z,i^*j_*\mathcal F)\longrightarrow\ .
$$

In particular, because the finite-boundary term is concentrated in
degree zero, the degree-one segment is

$$
H_c^0(Z,i^*j_*\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H_c^1(U,\mathcal F)
\longrightarrow H_c^1(C,j_*\mathcal F)\longrightarrow0
$$

and the degree-zero injection
$H_c^0(U,\mathcal F)\hookrightarrow H_c^0(C,j_*\mathcal F)$.

proof.text: Use the finite-field, separated finite-type smooth-curve and lisse coefficient conventions of [def-wf-middle-extension]. The base field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and itself), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $C_0$ Noetherian. Density of $U_0$ implies that its closed complement contains no generic point of an irreducible component: an open dense subset meets each component and hence contains its generic point. If two distinct points of $Z_0$ formed a strict specialization chain, adjoining a generic point of a component containing the first would give a length-two chain in the one-dimensional $C_0$. Thus $\dim Z_0\leq0$. Apply [lem-pc-zero-dimensional-closed-subscheme-finite] to $Z_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ to conclude that $Z_0$ is finite over $k_0$. This also covers the empty complement.

source.place: Tag 06LH (lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0), algebraic case; dimension-chain argument written here

proof.text: Put $A=j_*\mathcal F$, always the ordinary sheaf direct image of [def-wf-middle-extension], placed in degree zero. Apply [lem-a1-adic-middle-extension-constructible] to $j_0$ and $\mathcal F$. The hypotheses are exactly the dense open immersion of separated finite-type smooth curves, the lisse adic $\Qlb$-Weil coefficient convention, and the reduced closed complement of the statement. It gives $A\in\Sh_c(C,\Qlb)$ with its natural Weil structure. Thus $A$ is a permitted constructible input to recollement. This step does not identify the full derived direct image with an ordinary sheaf.

The restriction $j^*A$ is canonically $\mathcal F$. For an object $V$ of the site of $U$, regarded as an object over $C$, the ordinary direct-image formula of [def-wf-middle-extension] gives $(j_*\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(V\times_C U)=\mathcal F(V)$, because $V$ already factors through the open subscheme $U$. These equalities commute with restrictions and coefficient actions and are natural in $\mathcal F$, giving the sheaf isomorphism with its Weil structure.

Set $B=i^*A$. The boundary clause of [lem-a1-adic-middle-extension-constructible] makes $B$ a constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf in degree zero. Apply [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages] at $\Lambda=\Qlb$ to the constructible Weil complex $K=A$ on $C$. The schemes and complementary immersions are geometric base changes from $k_0$, so its equivariance clause applies. Using $j^*A=\mathcal F$ from step 3 gives
$$j_!\mathcal F\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow i_*B\longrightarrow j_!\mathcal F[1].$$
The theorem identifies $i_*=Ri_*$ in this triangle and makes all three arrows Weil-equivariant. The middle vertex remains the ordinary sheaf $A$.

Let $a_C:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism. Clause (3) of [prop-functor-package], applied to $f=a_C$ and $K=A$, gives the distinguished triangle
$$R(a_Cj)_!\mathcal F\longrightarrow R(a_C)_!A\longrightarrow R(a_Ci)_!B\longrightarrow .$$
Its hypotheses hold: the curves are separated and finite type, and $i,j$ are complementary immersions. Apply the point fibre functor, which carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles by [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence]. The definition [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] identifies the result with
$$R\Gamma_c(U,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(C,j_*\mathcal F)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(Z,i^*j_*\mathcal F)\longrightarrow .$$

Step 1 gives the finite structure morphism $Z_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$, and step 4 gives a $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf $B$ on $Z_0$. Therefore [lem-a1-finite-boundary-cohomology] applies, without a purity or weight hypothesis, and yields $H_c^r(Z,B)=0$ for every integer $r\ne0$. In particular $H_c^{-1}(Z,B)=H_c^1(Z,B)=0$.

By [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category] the distinguished triangle of step 5 in $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$ is isomorphic to the image under the stage functor $J_L$ of a distinguished triangle of $D(L)$ with vertices in $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(L)$, for some finite extension $L/\Ql$ inside $\Qlb$, and cohomology satisfies $H^i(T_{L'/L}X)\cong H^i(X)\otimes_LL'$ along the scalar-extension functors. Apply clause (5) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] to the standard t-structure of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] on $D(L)$, whose $H^i$ are the usual cohomology $L$-vector spaces, and extend scalars from $L$ to $\Qlb$, which is exact. The long exact sequence of compact-support cohomology so obtained contains
$$H_c^{-1}(Z,B)\longrightarrow H_c^0(U,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H_c^0(C,A)$$
and
$$H_c^0(Z,B)\xrightarrow{\delta}H_c^1(U,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{g}H_c^1(C,A)\longrightarrow H_c^1(Z,B).$$
No Frobenius compatibility of these maps is asserted or used: the statement concerns the coefficient complexes of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], computed on the underlying complexes.

source.place: Example 1.3.2(i), Theorem 1.3.6: standard t-structure and cohomological functor

proof.text: Substitute the two vanishings from step 6 in the exact sequences of step 7. Exactness with zero preceding term makes the kernel of $H_c^0(U,\mathcal F)\to H_c^0(C,A)$ zero, proving injectivity. Exactness at $H_c^1(U,\mathcal F)$ says $\operatorname{im}\delta=\ker g$, and exactness at $H_c^1(C,A)$ with zero following term says $\operatorname{im}g=H_c^1(C,A)$. This is the displayed degree-one exact segment ending in zero.

No Mathlib match for either geometric assertion.
split_report.blueprint: Current blueprint proof first sentence: steps 1-5 (ordinary middle extension, recollement and compact cohomology). Finite-boundary sentence: step 6. Final long-exact-sequence sentence: steps 7-8. This realizes the localization tool used in unit sk-i-dl-a1-local, preserving its local-duality and ramification route.

Only clause (5), the general long exact sequence of t-structure cohomology, is applied to coefficient complexes.
